scope: Proposition 4.5 of the manuscript “Randomized quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Randomized-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4ab7552f58266134), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every permitted Solve input, the execution and all its subroutine executions terminate on every random tape. The outputs of Solve and Ask are integer vectors in their respective input boxes. The outputs of Orient and OrientPlus have the stated choice and list types, and each listed set has input measure at most 1/2. Moreover: (i) Tightening makes at most 8ns updates and 16ns + 2 calls to Ask. (ii) A chain of main Solve continuations contains at most K = 8s(g + 1) + 1 (4.2) solver invocations. (iii) One Orient trial visits at most g + 1 orientation invocations and returns at most 2g + 2 sets. Consequently OrientPlus returns at most J(2g + 2) sets, counting repetitions.
